hook.en: In (x + 1/x)¹⁰ the x's in one term can cancel completely, leaving a pure number. Finding that term is a favourite exam question.
hook.kn: (x + 1/x)¹⁰ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಪದದ x ಗಳು ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣವಾಗಿ ರದ್ದಾಗಿ ಕೇವಲ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಉಳಿಯಬಹುದು. ಆ ಪದ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ಮೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ.

title.en: Find the term independent of x

say.en: In (x plus 1 over x) to the power 10 the x's in one term can cancel completely, leaving a pure number. Finding that term is a favourite exam question. In this lesson: Find the middle terms.
Find the term independent of x.

body.en: If $n$ is even, $(a + b)^n$ has an odd number $n + 1$ of terms and one middle term, $T_{n/2 + 1}$. If $n$ is odd, there are two *middle terms*, $T_{(n+1)/2}$ and $T_{(n+3)/2}$. In $(x + 1/x)^{2m}$ the middle term is the constant ${}^{2m}C_m$.
body.kn: n ಸಮ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಾದರೆ ಒಂದೇ ಮಧ್ಯ ಪದ T₍ₙ/₂₊₁₎; n ಬೆಸ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಾದರೆ ಎರಡು ಮಧ್ಯ ಪದಗಳು.

narration.en: For even n there is one middle term, term number n by two plus one. For odd n there are two middle terms.

say.en: For even n there is one middle term, term number n by two plus one. For odd n there are two middle terms. n even: T(n over 2 plus 1).

x plus 1 over x, to the 6, has 7 terms. The 4th is the middle and it is a constant.
Constant term of x squared plus 1 over x, to the 9: collect the power of x.
So the 7th term, 9 C 6, which is 84, is independent of x.

body.en: Write $T_{r+1}$, collect all powers of $x$ into a single $x^{\text{(expression in } r)}$, and set the exponent equal to 0. If $r$ comes out a whole number between 0 and $n$, substitute it; otherwise there is no such term.

n equals 10 is even: 11 terms, middle term T 6 r equals 5.

problem.en: Find the term independent of x in (x² − 2/x)⁶.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the term independent of x in (x² − 2/x)⁶.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the term independent of x in (x squared minus 2 over x) to the power 6.
T r plus 1 equals to the power 6C r x squared to the power 6 to the power -r (minus 2 over x) to the power r equals to the power 6C r minus 2 to the power r x to the power 12 to the power minus 3r.
12 minus 3r equals 0 so r equals 4.
T 5 equals to the power 6C 4 times 16 equals 15 times 16 equals 240.
So the answer is 240.

say.en: Shortcut for the constant term. For (x to the power p plus c over x^q) to the power n the constant term has r equals pn over p plus q. Example: (x squared plus 1 over x) to the power 9: r equals 18 over 3 equals 6, giving to the power 9C 6 equals 84.
